title: Module quiz: Scenario: conversational AI assistant

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: a conversational assistant for a book shop that remembers customers and hands over to people. The prompt tells the assistant to hand over on any sign of distress, and the team finds three missed signals in a week. What is the first fix?

options.text: Add three more examples of distress to the system prompt, in capitals
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt is a request that the model weighs, and the rule that must hold belongs in code: "a prompt is a request that a model weighs"

options.text: Route such messages in code before the model sees them
Raise the assistant's confidence threshold before it answers anything
options.says: Ruled out because a confidence threshold is the model's own judgement: "It fails because it makes a probabilistic judgement the only barrier on the one decision that must not be missed".

options.text: Ask the model to rate every customer message for distress and hand over above a score
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "What the design must not do is make the model the only layer."

questions.stem: Scenario: a conversational assistant for a book shop that remembers customers and hands over to people. A returning shopper is greeted with an address saved 200 days ago, and the policy limit is thirty days. What should the assistant do first?

options.text: Use it as it stands, treating a saved address as the best evidence there is
options.says: Ruled out because an old fact is not trusted: "a fact that has not been touched for months is more likely to be wrong than one from last week".

options.text: Use it and ask the account holder about it at the end of the call
options.says: Ruled out because an old fact is verified before use: "so that the assistant asks the customer before it relies on an address from last year".

options.text: Delete every stored fact older than the limit without telling anyone
options.says: Ruled out because an old fact is marked for checking and not discarded: "the example marks each fact `current` when it is no older than a limit, and `verify` when it is older".

options.text: Have the account holder confirm it before relying on it
options.says: An old fact is checked with the account holder before it is relied on: "an old fact is verified before it is used".

questions.stem: Scenario: a conversational assistant for a book shop that remembers customers and hands over to people. A segment of three conversations has none resolved by the assistant, the floor is 80 percent and the minimum is three. What does the review say about it?

options.text: It is weak, since the sample suffices and the result misses the bar
options.says: A segment at the minimum and below the floor is weak.

options.text: It is not weak, since three conversations are too few to judge
options.says: Ruled out because the minimum is met: "two unresolved conversations prove nothing and three begin to".

options.text: It is not weak yet, since a fourth conversation must confirm the pattern
options.says: Ruled out because the minimum is a floor and not a margin: "only when it has at least a minimum number of conversations".

options.text: It is not weak, since a person settled some of the conversations
options.says: Ruled out because a settlement by a person is not the assistant's: "A conversation that a person settled is a good outcome and is not the assistant's."

questions.stem: Scenario: a conversational assistant for a book shop that remembers customers and hands over to people. A conversation with forty turns ends in a stalled hand-off. Is it counted as overlong?

options.text: Yes, since forty turns is above any sensible limit
options.says: Ruled out because the length alone is not the test: "A conversation with more turns than the limit and no hand-off."

options.text: Yes, because a stall proves that the assistant should have stopped earlier
options.says: Ruled out because the stall is a hand-off: "A conversation that was handed over is not overlong, because somebody took over."

options.text: No, since a person took over
options.says: A hand-over takes the conversation out of the measure.

options.text: No, because stalled hand-offs are excluded from every figure in the review
options.says: Ruled out because a hand-off still enters the escalation counts: "A hand-off nobody needed and that had no safety signal behind it is over-escalation, and a conversation that needed a person and never got one is under-escalation. Both are counted".
